docs.title: Technical Reference: WebSocket Gateway Telemetry
docs.text: This document outlines the message protocols and event lifecycle for the FastAPI WebSocket Gateway located at /ws/stream.

docs.title: 1. Connection Lifecycle
docs.text:
Clients establish a persistent bi-directional connection: 

ws://localhost:8000/ws/stream?token=<optional_jwt>

Authentication is optional for anonymous exploration, but required for saving permanent taste embeddings to a user profile.

docs.title: 2. Event Types & Payloads
docs.text:
The gateway emits JSON messages with the following standard envelope:

{
  "type": "STAGE_UPDATE | PARTIAL_DATA | HUMAN_INTERRUPTION | COMPLETED | ERROR",
  "stage": "PARSING_TICKETS | EXTRACTING_CONSTRAINTS | SCORING_POIS | SOLVING_TSPTW | DONE",
  "message": "Human-readable status text",
  "payload": {}
}

docs.title: 2.1. STAGE_UPDATE
docs.text:
Emitted as the LangGraph state machine transitions between nodes:

Stage Triggering Node Description PARSING_TICKETS ticket_parser_node Pydantic AI is extracting flight and hotel anchors from raw text. EXTRACTING_CONSTRAINTS assemble_constraints_node Compiling temporal boundaries and budgets deterministically. VERIFYING_CONSTRAINTS verify_constraints_node Reviewing extracted anchors and collecting missing fields. EVALUATING_GUARDRAILS guardrails_node Validating logical boundaries and querying DB schedule overlaps. ANALYZING_PROMPT prompt_analyzer_node Extracting taste affinities and preferred cuisines via Ollama. SCORING_POIS planner_scrape_node Batch encoding POIs into 16-D tensors and computing ML scores. SOLVING_TSPTW planner_optimize_node Executing the C++ branch-and-bound optimization solver.

docs.title: A. Constraints Verification (type: "VERIFICATION_REQUIRED")
docs.text:
Emitted when user review or missing parameter collection is required:

{
  "event": "VERIFICATION_REQUIRED",
  "status": "awaiting_input",
  "data": {
    "type": "VERIFICATION_REQUIRED",
    "message": "Review and verify extracted trip constraints.",
    "fields": ["budget_usd"],
    "constraints": { ... },
    "booking_anchors": { ... }
  }
}

Resume Request: 

{
  "action": "resume",
  "answers": {
    "budget_usd": 2000.0,
    "origin_city": "Madrid",
    "destination_city": "Paris"
  }
}

docs.title: B. Schedule Overlap Warning (type: "TRIP_OVERLAP_WARNING")
docs.text:
Emitted when trip dates collide with an existing trip in PostgreSQL:

{
  "event": "TRIP_OVERLAP_WARNING",
  "status": "warning",
  "data": {
    "type": "TRIP_OVERLAP_WARNING",
    "message": "Trip schedule overlap detected with existing trip to Paris.",
    "warning_title": "[WARNING] TRIP SCHEDULE OVERLAP",
    "overlapping_trip": {
      "destination": "Paris",
      "start_date": "2026-10-10",
      "end_date": "2026-10-15"
    },
    "variant": "warning"
  }
}

Resume Request: - Proceed: {"action": "resume", "approved": true, "proceed": true} - Abort: {"action": "resume", "approved": false, "abort": true}

docs.title: 2.3. COMPLETED
docs.text:
Emitted when the C++ solver converges and the final itinerary is ready:

{
  "type": "COMPLETED",
  "stage": "DONE",
  "message": "Itinerary optimized successfully!",
  "payload": {
    "itinerary": {
      "days": [
        {
          "day_index": 1,
          "date": "2026-10-12",
          "stops": [...],
          "total_cost_eur": 45.0,
          "total_score": 382.4
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 1. Overview & Goals
docs.text: This document outlines the architectural design for a client-side notification system in Paladio's Next.js frontend. The system provides: - User-Isolated Storage: Notifications are partitioned per authenticated user (user.id) in localStorage. - Hybrid Triggering: Automatic capture of engine/WebSocket telemetry events (solver completion, errors, clarification requests) alongside a simple imperative notify API for React components and user actions. - Rich Timestamps: Every notification includes an ISO timestamp formatted into readable date & time plus relative time indicators. - Interactive UI Surfaces: A notification bell with unread badge in the sidebar/navigation, a slide-out/dropdown notification center with read/clear controls and actionable links, and transient floating toasts for real-time alerts.

docs.title: 2.1 Type Definitions (frontend/src/types/notification.ts)
docs.text:
export type NotificationType = 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error';

export interface NotificationItem {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  type: NotificationType;
  title: string;
  message: string;
  timestamp: string; // ISO 8601 (e.g., "2026-09-16T17:40:00.000Z")
  read: boolean;
  actionLink?: string; // e.g., "/engine", "/vault"
  actionLabel?: string; // e.g., "View Itinerary"
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export interface ToastItem {
  id: string;
  notification: NotificationItem;
  durationMs: number;
}

docs.title: 2.2 Storage Isolation Strategy
docs.text:
• Key Schema: paladio_notifications_${userId}. If no user is logged in, fallback to paladio_notifications_guest.
  • User Switching: When user in AuthContext changes:
  • The active storage key is updated.
  • The store rehydrates with the new user's notification list.
  • No cross-user data leakage is possible.
  • Quota & Retention Policy:
  • Maximum 100 notifications per user.
  • Automatically drops the oldest notifications when limit is reached (FIFO).
  • Storage operations are wrapped in try/catch to handle private browsing or quota limits gracefully.

docs.title: 3.1 Store: useNotificationStore (frontend/src/stores/notificationStore.ts)
docs.text:
Built using Zustand (^5.0.15):

interface NotificationState {
  currentUserId: string | null;
  notifications: NotificationItem[];
  toasts: ToastItem[];
  unreadCount: number;

  // Actions
  initUser: (userId: string | null) => void;
  addNotification: (params: Omit<NotificationItem, 'id' | 'timestamp' | 'read' | 'userId'>) => NotificationItem;
  markAsRead: (id: string) => void;
  markAllAsRead: () => void;
  removeNotification: (id: string) => void;
  clearAll: () => void;
  dismissToast: (toastId: string) => void;
}

docs.title: 3.2 Imperative Dispatcher API (frontend/src/utils/notify.ts)
docs.text:
A clean helper for components: 

export const notify = {
  info: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
  success: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
  warning: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
  error: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
};

docs.title: 4.1 Bridge Hook: useSocketNotificationBridge (frontend/src/hooks/useSocketNotificationBridge.ts)
docs.text:
Subscribes to telemetry from SocketContext or wraps the socket handler to generate relevant alerts: - EVALUATING_ROUTES (status completed / recovered): Emits success notification: "Itinerary Generated — Route and transit plan is ready." with action link to /engine or /vault. - CLARIFICATION_NEEDED: Emits warning notification: "Input Required — Solver requires additional constraints." with action link to /engine. - ERROR: Emits error notification: "Engine Fault — Inference failed." - FEEDBACK_PROCESSED: Emits info notification: "Preference Model Updated".

Duplicate suppression is built-in so re-renders or socket reconnects do not trigger duplicate notifications.

docs.title: 5.1 Notification Bell & Unread Badge (NotificationBell.tsx)
docs.text:
• Placed in Sidebar.tsx (or top navigation).
  • Shows an indicator badge with unread count (e.g. 3 or 9+).
  • Clicking toggles the Notification Center panel.

docs.title: 5.2 Notification Center (NotificationCenter.tsx)
docs.text:
• Slide-out drawer or anchored popover dropdown.
  • Header displaying total notifications and "Mark all as read" / "Clear all" buttons.
  • List displaying:
  • Type icon / badge (Color-coded: blue, green, amber, red).
  • Title and message text.
  • Formatted date & time (e.g., Sep 16, 17:40) and relative time (5m ago).
  • Action button/link if actionLink is present.
  • Delete (trash) icon to dismiss individual item.
  • Read/unread dot toggle.
  • Empty state: "No notifications yet."

docs.title: 5.3 Toast Container & Toast Card (ToastContainer.tsx)
docs.text:
• Fixed at the top-right (z-index: 9999).
  • Displays animated entrance/exit.
  • Auto-dismisses after 4 seconds (configurable).
  • Includes close x button and link button if applicable.

docs.title: 6. Testing & Verification
docs.text:
1. Unit Tests:
  2. Store persistence: Verify adding a notification writes to localStorage under paladio_notifications_${userId}.
  3. User switching: Verify switching userId loads only that user's notifications.
  4. Cap enforcement: Verify exceeding 100 items evicts the oldest.
  5. Mark as read, remove, clear all operations.
  6. Component & Integration Tests:
  7. Verify NotificationBell updates badge on new notifications.

docs.title: Design Specification: Paladio Core Open-Source Showcase & Architecture Documentation
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-09-23
  • Author: Paladio Core Systems & Operations Research Team
  • Target Repository: Leandro-Juan/paladio-core (synchronized from cpp_core/ via GitHub Actions)
  • Primary Goal: Transform paladio-core into an elite, production-grade, star-worthy public repository with comprehensive Diátaxis documentation, empirical benchmarks, Apache 2.0 license, and modern C++/Python packaging.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Value Proposition
docs.text:
paladio-core is an ultra-fast, deterministic C++20 engine with zero-copy Python (pybind11) bindings designed to solve the Time-Constrained Orienteering Problem with Time Windows (TCOPTW), budget constraints, and real-world human travel constraints.

Combinatorial routing with budget and time windows is strongly NP-hard. Exploring all permutations on an \(N\)-node graph requires \(O(N!)\) operations, making naive depth-first search infeasible for \(N > 10\). paladio-core achieves microsecond-to-millisecond execution times by combining: 1. Continuous Fractional Knapsack Upper Bounding: An admissible linear relaxation that computes an upper bound on remaining score in \(O(N)\) at each search node, pruning subtrees that cannot surpass the incumbent solution. 2. Compact 64-Bit Bitmask State Encoding: Node visitation, mandatory milestones, and category sets are stored as bit patterns in uint64_t registers, enabling \(O(1)\) operations with hardware intrinsics (std::countr_zero). 3. Dominance Pruning & State Memoization: Multi-criteria Pareto-dominance pruning that eliminates paths that arrive later, at higher cost, or with lower score than previously explored trajectories for equivalent visited subsets. 4. Zero-Allocation Hot-Path Architecture: Zero dynamic memory allocations (malloc/new) inside the core branch-and-bound recursion, ensuring maximum cache locality and deterministic low latency.

  • Guided Heuristic Search: Explains that when non-linear human realism constraints are enabled (fatigue decay curves, meal scheduling windows, pacing penalties, and diminishing returns on category monotony), the relaxation transitions gracefully into a guided heuristic Branch-and-Bound search that prunes unpromising branches while respecting complex real-world bounds.

docs.title: 3.4. Zero-Allocation Hot-Path Architecture Callout
docs.text:
A prominent callout highlighting systems engineering excellence:

High-Performance Architecture Highlights: - \(O(1)\) State Transitions: Node visitation bitmasks and category histories are tracked in 64-bit unsigned integers (uint64_t), utilizing compiler and CPU intrinsics (std::countr_zero). - Zero Heap Allocation in Hot Loops: DFS call frames, path tracking (std::array<int, 64>), and category counts (std::array<uint8_t, 8>) reside on contiguous stack memory without calling malloc or new during branch exploration. - Sanitizer Clean: 100% verified under Clang/GCC AddressSanitizer (ASan), LeakSanitizer (LSan), and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (UBSan). - GIL-Free Concurrency: Python bindings release the Global Interpreter Lock (pybind11::gil_scoped_release), allowing pure multi-threaded C++ scaling across CPU cores.

docs.title: Design Specification: Global TSPTW with Soft Time-Window Constraints
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-16 Status: Approved Author: Antigravity

docs.title: 1. Context & Motivation
docs.text:
Previously, re-optimizing an itinerary day partitioned the sequence into isolated sub-tours bounded by fixed anchors (hotels, airports, or user-locked POIs). While this prevented locked items from moving, it fragmented the global optimization problem into piecewise sub-problems. If a user locked a stop at mid-day, the solver could not optimize across the boundary, causing artificial zig-zagging and sub-optimal overall routes.

This specification designs a unified global Traveling Salesperson Problem with Time Windows (TSPTW) solver in C++20 (paladio_core), replacing piecewise array partitioning with soft time-window constraints \([t_{\text{target}} - \epsilon, t_{\text{target}} + \epsilon]\).

docs.title: 2.1 Graph & Node Attributes
docs.text: Let \(G = (V, E)\) be a complete directed graph with \(n = |V|\) POIs, and transit duration matrix \(T \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^{n \times n}\). Each vertex \(i \in V\) is associated with: - \(D_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\): Dwell duration (minutes). - \([W_i^{\min}, W_i^{\max}]\): Permissible arrival window (minutes from midnight). - For locked POIs at scheduled arrival time \(t_{\text{target}}\): $\(W_i^{\min} = \max(t_{\text{day\_start}}, t_{\text{target}} - \epsilon), \quad W_i^{\max} = \min(t_{\text{day\_end}}, t_{\text{target}} + \epsilon)\)$ Default \(\epsilon = 15\) minutes (30-minute arrival window). - For unlocked POIs: $\(W_i^{\min} = \max(t_{\text{day\_start}}, \text{earliest\_time}_i), \quad W_i^{\max} = \min(t_{\text{day\_end}}, \text{latest\_time}_i)\)$ - For the start depot (node 0, e.g. morning hotel): $\(W_0^{\min} = W_0^{\max} = t_{\text{day\_start}}\)$ - For a fixed end depot (node \(n-1\), e.g. night hotel return): Fixed at permutation index \(n-1\).

docs.title: 2.2 Forward Timeline Simulation
docs.text: For any tour permutation \(\pi = (\pi_0, \pi_1, \dots, \pi_{n-1})\): 1. Initialize arrival and departure at start depot: $\(t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_0) = W_{\pi_0}^{\min}, \quad t_{\text{dep}}(\pi_0) = t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_0) + D_{\pi_0}\)$ 2. For \(k = 1, \dots, n-1\): $\(t_{\text{transit}} = T[\pi_{k-1}, \pi_k]\)$ $\(t_{\text{reach}} = t_{\text{dep}}(\pi_{k-1}) + t_{\text{transit}}\)$ $\(t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_k) = \max(t_{\text{reach}}, W_{\pi_k}^{\min})\)$ $\(t_{\text{dep}}(\pi_k) = t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_k) + D_{\pi_k}\)$

docs.title: 2.3 Soft Penalty Objective
docs.text: $\(\text{Cost}(\pi) = \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} T[\pi_{k-1}, \pi_k] + \lambda_{\text{penalty}} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left( \max(0, t_{\text{reach}}(\pi_k) - W_{\pi_k}^{\max}) \right)^2\)$ Where: - \(\lambda_{\text{penalty}} = 100.0\): Heavily penalizes arriving after \(W^{\max}\), driving the solver to meet locked windows without discarding candidates. - Idling before \(W^{\min}\) is accounted for in \(t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_k) = \max(t_{\text{reach}}, W_{\pi_k}^{\min})\) without extra penalty, representing natural waiting time.

docs.title: 3.1 Function Signature (cpp_core/include/paladio/engine.hpp)
docs.text:
[[nodiscard]] std::vector<int> solve_tsptw(
    const int *transit_durations, int n,
    const int *dwell_times,
    const int *window_starts,
    const int *window_ends,
    int start_node = 0,
    int end_node = -1,
    bool fixed_end = false,
    double penalty_weight = 100.0);

docs.title: 3.2 Optimization Engine (cpp_core/src/engine.cpp)
docs.text:
1. Initial Solution Generation:
  2. Multi-start greedy heuristic combining nearest neighbor with earliest deadline sorting (\(W_i^{\min}\)).
  3. Generates up to 8 diverse valid starting permutations.
  4. Local Search Improvements:
  5. 2-Opt Edge Inversion: Iteratively reverses tour sub-sequences \([\pi_i, \dots, \pi_j]\) whenever the total cost (transit + window penalty) decreases.
  6. Or-Opt Node Relocation: Relocates single nodes and consecutive pairs to candidate insertion slots that minimize cost.
  7. Performance & Determinism Guarantees:
  8. Zero heap allocation in hot loop (pre-allocated working arrays).
  9. Worst-case execution time under 10ms for \(n \le 25\).
  10. Releases Python GIL via pybind11::gil_scoped_release.

docs.title: 4.1 Pybind11 Binding (cpp_core/src/bindings.cpp)
docs.text: Expose solve_tsptw taking flattened 1D numpy arrays for durations, dwell_times, window_starts, window_ends, integers n, start_node, end_node, boolean fixed_end, and float penalty_weight.

docs.title: 4.2 Reoptimization Service (backend/app/services/trip_reoptimization_service.py)
docs.text:
1. In reoptimize_trip_slice:
  2. Inspect items of the target day.
  3. For each item, compute dwell duration and time windows \([W^{\min}, W^{\max}]\) based on locked status.
  4. If locked: center tight window around current scheduled start (\(t \pm \epsilon\)).
  5. If unlocked: set window to operating hours or \([t_{\text{day\_start}}, t_{\text{day\_end}}]\).
  6. Call paladio_core.solve_tsptw(...) over the entire day's nodes in one single call.
  7. Reconstruct the day's timeline with arrival/departure times.

docs.title: 1. Context & Motivation
docs.text:
Currently, Paladio's route monitoring pipeline only tracks unidirectional outbound flights (origin_iata -> destination_code). When a user monitors a corridor like Madrid (MAD) to Berlin (BER), only outbound flight ticks are ingested, stored, and plotted in the Price Trend Graph and Multi-Month Price Matrix. Furthermore, the proactive deal detection engine calculates package savings by combining outbound ticks with estimated lodging, omitting actual return flight pricing.

This specification designs: 1. Bi-directional Corpus Ingestion: Ingesting and maintaining price baselines for both outbound (A -> B) and return (B -> A) flights. 2. Dual-Trend Price Graph: Simultaneous rendering of Outbound and Return forward curves / historical prices, with a quick segment toggle ([ BOTH ] [ OUTBOUND ] [ RETURN ]). 3. Multi-Month Round-Trip Calendar Matrix: - Direction toggles: [ OUTBOUND ] [ RETURN ] [ BEST ROUND-TRIP ]. - Pricing sub-toggle for Round-Trip mode: [ FLIGHTS ONLY ] [ FLIGHT + HOTEL ]. - Horizon toggle limited strictly to [ 4M ] and [ FULL HORIZON ] (up to 11 months). - Departure-indexed cells with automatic cheapest return pairing across [min_nights, max_nights]. - Hover and selection range bar highlighting stay duration on the calendar grid. - Drawer with complete flight pairing details, lodging breakdown, direct booking links, and a direct "Plan Itinerary" action. 4. Deal Detection Engine Enhancement: Requiring confirmed, lowest-cost return flights in deal candidate packages.

docs.title: 3.1 Dual-Corpus Ingestion & Celery Tasks
docs.text:
In backend/app/engine/market/corpus.py: - backfill_route_corpus is updated to accept an optional bidirectional: bool = True parameter (default True). - When backfilling route (origin_iata, destination_code), it automatically backfills both: 1. origin_iata -> destination_code 2. destination_code -> origin_iata - RouteCorpusStatusModel maintains health and departure date counts for each directed pair.

In backend/app/engine/market/detector.py: - run_deal_detection_scan() pairs each outbound flight tick ft with matching return flight ticks rt from destination_code -> origin_iata where rt.depart_date == ft.depart_date + timedelta(days=nights). - If no return flight exists for that date, candidate is disqualified or penalized, ensuring verified round trips.

Accepts query parameters: - view: "outbound" | "inbound" | "roundtrip" (default: "outbound") - pricing: "flights" | "package" (default: "flights") - months: int (validated to either 4 or 11, default: 4)

Response schema includes return flight details and lodging breakdown:

docs.text:
• Adds a segment toggle: [ BOTH ] [ OUTBOUND ] [ RETURN ].
  • In BOTH mode, plots two lines on the same Cartesian grid:

  • Return curve: Accent Purple (#A855F7)

docs.title: 4.2 Route Monitoring Calendar (MonitoringCalendar.tsx)
docs.text:
• Strictly scoped to Route Monitoring: Located at src/components/monitoring/MonitoringCalendar.tsx, distinct from the Trip Workspace Itinerary Calendar.
  • Horizon Selector: Replaces [3M] [4M] [5M] with:
  • [ 4M ]: 4 months view.
  • [ FULL HORIZON ]: Full price horizon (11 months).
  • View Navigation Bar:
  • [ OUTBOUND ]
  • [ RETURN ]
  • [ BEST ROUND-TRIP ]
  • Pricing Mode (in BEST ROUND-TRIP mode):
  • Sub-toggle buttons: [ FLIGHTS ONLY ] and [ FLIGHT + HOTEL ].
  • Stay Interval Visualizer:
  • When hovering or clicking an active departure day \(D_{out}\) with duration \(N\), calendar days from \(D_{out}\) to \(D_{out} + N\) are decorated with an active range band class (styles.inRangeDay).
  • Inspection Drawer:
  • Outbound flight card (departure time, duration, flight number, booking link).
  • Return flight card (return date, departure time, duration, flight number, booking link).
  • Optional Hotel card (nightly average, total lodging).
  • Prominent tactical action button: [ PLAN ITINERARY WITH THESE DATES ], which navigates to /trips/new (or triggers trip generation) prefilled with origin, destination, and selected departure/return dates.

docs.title: 5. Error Handling & Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Missing Return Flight Data: If no return flight is available for a given departure day within [min_nights, max_nights], that cell is marked as "no_data", rather than showing a broken or partial price.
  • Rate Limiting & Provider Health: Ingesting both directions doubles API requests to the provider. The ingestion worker employs jittered backoff and respects provider quota limits.
  • Air-Gapped & Offline Fallback: Baselines are drawn from stored PostgreSQL ticks without external cloud API dependencies.

docs.title: First Autonomous Swarm Trip
docs.text: In this tutorial, you will plan a trip using Paladio's Active Engine cockpit (/engine), configure travel constraints and anchors, stream real-time WebSocket telemetry from the multi-agent swarm, and inspect the converged combinatorial itinerary.

docs.title: 1. Navigating to the Active Engine Cockpit
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to: 

http://localhost:3000/engine
Or click Active Engine in the sidebar navigation.

The Active Engine interface is structured into two main workspaces: - 01 // MISSION PREPARATION: Configuration interface for prompt intent, budget, meal windows, and flight/hotel anchors. - 02 // TELEMETRY CONSOLE: Live streaming terminal and output panel (OUTPUT TELEMETRY) powered by persistent WebSockets.

docs.title: 2. Configuring the Travel Parameters (01 // MISSION PREPARATION)
docs.text: In the Mission Preparation tab, set up your trip parameters:

docs.title: Step 2.1: Trip Intent & Preferences
docs.text:
In the > TRIP INTENT & PREFERENCES textarea, define your qualitative travel goals:

"Visit the main cultural landmarks and museums. Love traditional bistros and relaxed cafes."

This prompt is analyzed by the sovereign local LLM (prompt_analyzer) to update your continuous 768-D taste vector and extract domain category affinities.

docs.title: Step 2.2: Financial Budget Ceiling
docs.text:
In > BUDGET CEILING, enter your currency envelope: 

$ 1500 USD
The C++ solver uses this constraint to enforce a strict upper bound on POI admission fees and transit legs.

docs.title: Step 2.3: Mandatory Meal Windows
docs.text:
Under > MEAL CONSTRAINTS, review the culturally calibrated meal windows: - Breakfast: 08:00 \(\rightarrow\) 10:00 - Lunch: 12:00 \(\rightarrow\) 14:30 - Dinner: 19:30 \(\rightarrow\) 22:00

You can click + ADD MEAL WINDOW (e.g., for an afternoon snack) or adjust the boundary hours. The solver treats these as hard temporal time windows where food venues must be scheduled.

docs.title: Step 2.4: Travel Anchors (Flights & Hotel)
docs.text:
Paladio anchors itineraries around real flight arrival/departure times and lodging locations. Select your mode:

  • Simulated Anchors (Test Mode):
  • Origin City: Madrid
  • Destination City: Paris
  • Automated Generation: Generates round-trip flight bookings between real IATA airports (MAD \(\rightarrow\) CDG) and verifies a hotel in the destination city for 5 days.
  • Direct Ticket Ingestion (Production Mode):
  • Paste raw flight confirmation text, boarding passes, or hotel vouchers directly into the intake box for deterministic parsing by the Pydantic AI ticket_parser agent.

docs.title: 3. Initializing the Solver & Streaming Telemetry
docs.text:
Click the blue INITIALIZE SOLVER [MADRID -> PARIS] button at the bottom of the form.

The interface immediately switches to 02 // TELEMETRY CONSOLE and the OUTPUT TELEMETRY panel connects via WebSockets (/api/v1/ws/stream):

[PHASE: PARSER]      Extracting booking anchors...
                     -> Origin: Madrid (MAD) | Destination: Paris (CDG)
                     -> Hotel: Hotel Pullman Paris Tour Eiffel
                     -> Dates: 5-day optimization horizon
[PHASE: CONSTRAINTS] Deterministically assembling temporal & financial bounds...
                     -> Budget: $1500.00 USD
                     -> Hard Meal Windows: 3 daily (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner)
[PHASE: ANALYSIS]    Extracting travel tastes & tag affinities via Ollama...
                     -> High Affinities: art_culture (0.92), food_culinary (0.88)
[PHASE: ML_SCORING]  Batch encoding POIs into 16-D feature tensors...
                     -> Computing Bayesian smoothed ratings
                     -> Applying user taste EMA vector update
[PHASE: SOLVER]      Dispatching to C++ paladio-core branch-and-bound solver...
                     -> Evaluated 3,840 graph permutations in 1.86 ms
[PHASE: COMPLETED]   Optimal multi-day itinerary converged!

docs.title: 4. Inspecting and Saving the Results
docs.text: Once converged, the interface renders the interactive results in the right viewport:

docs.title: 1. The Daily Trip Timeline (TripTimeline)
docs.text:
• Day-by-Day Tabs: Navigate through each scheduled day.
  • Chronological Time Cards: Fixed POI visit windows (\([09:30, 11:30]\)) displaying attraction names, estimated admission costs, and categories.
  • Dedicated Meal Blocks: Culturally scheduled lunch and dinner venues.
  • Multimodal Transit Buffers: Walking and metro transit times with live fare estimates calculated between consecutive POIs.

docs.title: 2. Saving to Vault & Upcoming Trips
docs.text: Click the SAVE TRIP TO VAULT button in the header of the converged itinerary: - The itinerary is permanently saved to PostgreSQL. - You can now view and manage it under Upcoming Trips (/trips) and explore historical itineraries in the Itinerary Vault (/vault).

docs.title: 5. What Just Happened Under the Hood?
docs.text:
1. ticket_parser Agent: Verified flight timings and hotel check-in/out bounds using Pydantic AI models.
  2. assemble_constraints_node: Synthesized financial envelopes, meal windows, and spatial anchors into a validated TravelConstraints structure.
  3. prompt_analyzer Agent: Extracted semantic tastes and executed an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) update on your permanent 768-D latent vector.
  4. MLScorer: Encoded POIs in the destination city into 16-D tensors, computing Bayesian-smoothed multi-attribute utility scores.
  5. paladio-core (C++): Formulated and solved the Time-Constrained Orienteering Problem with Time Windows (TCOPTW) via branch-and-bound DFS and Knapsack bounding in sub-millisecond time.

Congratulations! You have completed your first autonomous swarm-optimized trip with Paladio.

docs.title: Quickstart with Docker
docs.text: In this 5-minute tutorial, you will launch the complete Paladio ecosystem locally using Docker Compose. Zero cloud subscriptions or external API keys are required.

docs.title: 1. System Requirements
docs.text: Before starting, ensure your system has: - Operating System: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora), macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel), or Windows (via WSL2). - Docker & Compose: Docker Engine 24.0+ and Docker Compose v2+. - RAM: Minimum 8 GB (16 GB recommended for concurrent local LLM inference). - Disk Space: ~10 GB free space for database storage and quantized model weights.

docs.title: 2. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the Paladio monorepo and navigate to its root:

git clone https://github.com/Leandro-Juan/Paladio.git
cd Paladio

docs.title: 3. Environment Configuration
docs.text:
Paladio uses standard 12-factor configuration via .env. A complete local development template is provided:

cp .env.example .env

The default .env is pre-configured to communicate seamlessly across the Docker network: - POSTGRES_HOST=postgres - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0 - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434/v1

docs.title: 4. Spin Up the Stack
docs.text:
Launch the container cluster in detached mode:

docker compose up -d

Docker will start the following coordinated services: 1. postgres: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector and TimescaleDB extensions. 2. redis: Redis 7 for task queuing, caching, and LangGraph checkpointer persistence. 3. ollama: Local LLM runtime hosting quantized models (qwen2.5 / llama3.1). 4. backend: FastAPI Semantic Gateway and Celery worker threads. 5. frontend: Next.js 15 web client with interactive maps and telemetry.

Verify that all containers are healthy:

docker compose ps

docs.title: 5. Verify the Installation
docs.text:
Once the containers are running, access the user-facing endpoints:

Service Local URL Description Next.js Web UI http://localhost:3000 Interactive dashboard, trip timeline, and affinity radar FastAPI Swagger Docs http://localhost:8000/docs REST API exploration and schema definitions WebSocket Gateway ws://localhost:8000/ws/stream Real-time bi-directional agent streaming endpoint

docs.title: 6. Next Steps
docs.text: Now that your sovereign stack is operational, proceed to the First Autonomous Swarm Trip tutorial to generate your first optimized itinerary.
